ART-03.note: Madhubani painting: Mithila region of Bihar, bold lines, intricate patterns, natural colours (NCERT lefa108 + PIB e-Auction 2025 release; claims c48, c73).
Bhimbetka rock shelters: Vindhya hills, Madhya Pradesh, about 45 km south of Bhopal, about 800 shelters / 500 painted, discovered 1957-58 by V.S. Wakankar (NCERT kefa101; claims c03, c04).
Bengal School of Art: began in Calcutta, associated with the Swadeshi movement, spearheaded by Abanindranath Tagore with E.B. Havell's support (NCERT lefa106; claim c62).
Kala Bhavana, Shantiniketan: India's first national art school, part of Visva-Bharati; Nandalal Bose invited to head the painting department (NCERT lefa106; claim c64).

Basohli (bold style, beetle-wing green) and Kangra (via the Guler / pre-Kangra phase) miniatures (NCERT lefa105; claims c42, c43). The bank item's Nadir Shah 1739 migration framing is not in the fetched NCERT text; the schools, sequence and features are taught.

Chola bronzes and the Nataraja icon are sculpture, not painting. This chapter teaches Chola-period painting only (Brihadeswara murals, claim c12); bronze casting is covered only for Dhokra (folk craft). Bronze/Nataraja iconography belongs to a sculpture/architecture chapter (ART-04 scope).

SNA ICH inventory crafts (Patola of Patan, Hingan plaques of Molela, Thatheras of Jandiala Guru, Kolam of Tamil Nadu): none of these four crafts appears in the sources fetched for this chapter (NCERT Living Art Traditions covers Dhokra and terracotta only). Source gap; not taught rather than asserted.

Mughal painter not mentioned by Abul Fazl (key: Mansur). The chapter teaches Abu'l Fazl on painting and Humayun's painters Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad from lehs205, but the Ain-i-Akbari painter list (Miskin, Mukund, Farrukh) and Mansur's Jahangir-era fame are not in any fetched source. NCERT lefa103/lefa104 could not be fetched on this machine. Source gap.

Who painted Bharat Mata (key: Abanindranath Tagore). Abanindranath and the Bengal School are taught, but the fetched NCERT lefa106 text does not mention the Bharat Mata painting specifically, so the specific work is not taught/asserted here.

Artist who did NOT belong to the Bengal School (key: Raja Ravi Varma). Taught explicitly: Ravi Varma belonged to the earlier Western academic tradition; Nandalal Bose and Abanindranath were Bengal School (claims c61, c62; exam_note in section).
Kalamkari painting originated in Andhra Pradesh (PIB Project PARI form-state list, claim c77; definition claim c74).

Portrait painting as the most significant contribution of Mughal painting. Taught via Mughal portraiture, including Abu'l Hasan's painting of Jahangir holding Akbar's portrait (claim c33) and the halo/portrait discussion (c31).
Jamini Roy was a famous painter (claims c66, c67: folk-inspired style, Bankura terracotta influence).
Term for an artwork painted directly onto a wall: mural. Taught as the mural (প্রাচীরচিত্র) tradition from Ajanta onwards; the English term 'Mural' is given in the chapter's terms list.
Mona Lisa's museum (Louvre, Paris): Western art history, outside this chapter's Indian painting scope and outside all allowed sources fetched. Not taught.
Who painted 'The Starry Night' (Van Gogh): Western art history, outside this chapter's scope and sources. Not taught.
Kalamkari refers to a hand-painted cotton textile tradition of South India (claim c74: hand painting on cotton or silk with a tamarind pen, natural dyes).

ART-04.note: Konarak Sun Temple as a solar chariot: twelve pairs of wheels, seven horses, jagamohana and nata-mandira taught from ASI + NCERT kefa106 (claims c37, c38, c21).
Qutb Minar: Aibak laid the foundation in AD 1199 and raised the first storey; Iltutmish added three storeys; height 72.5 m (claims c39, c40).
Khajuraho under the Chandellas: Lakshmana temple 954 (Dhanga), Kandariya Mahadeva largest (Ganda), 85 in tradition / 25 standing (claims c16, c45, c46, c47).
Hampi/Vijayanagara: southern bank of the Tungabhadra, monuments AD 1336-1570, Krishnadeva Raya, Vitthala temple (claims c48, c49, c50).
Nagara (north, curving shikhara) vs Dravida (south, pyramidal vimana) taught as the chapter's core distinction (claims c10, c11).
Vesara as the hybrid style popular after the mid-seventh century; Hoysala stellate plan and soapstone carving (claims c30, c31, c32).
Odisha temples: shikhara called deul, mandapa called jagamohana; lavish exterior, bare interior, boundary walls (claims c19, c20).
Mauryan art: Lomus Rishi cave donated by Ashoka for the Ajivikas, Dhauli rock-cut elephant with Ashokan edict, polished Didarganj Yakshi (claims c04, c05, c06).
Taj Mahal: built by Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal, char-bagh garden divided into four quarters, polychrome inlay (pietra dura-type) work taught (claims c51, c53, c56).
